---
title: "Randomized study on AI-assisted learning"
params:
  lang: "en"
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
library(exams)
library(mathml)
library(htmltools)
library(mistakes)

hook(s2_pool, subscript(s^2L, pool))
hook(mu_A, subscript(mean(X), "A"))
hook(mu_B, subscript(mean(X), "B"))
hook(n_A, subscript(n, "A"))
hook(n_B, subscript(n, "B"))
hook(s_A, subscript(s, "A"))
hook(s_B, subscript(s, "B"))

task <- "tgroups3"
plfile <- file.path("rexams", sprintf("%s.pl", task))
rolog::consult(system.file(plfile, package="mistakes"))


## DATA GENERATION
repeat
{
  n_A <- sample(20:50, 1)
  n_B <- n_A + sample(-10:10, 1)

  mu_A <- round(runif(1, 50, 75), 1)
  mu_B <- round(runif(1, 55, 85), 1)

  s_A <- round(runif(1, 8, 15), 1)
  s_B <- round(runif(1, 8, 15), 1)

  if(n_A == n_B)
    next

  s2_pool <- round(((n_A - 1) * s_A^2 + (n_B - 1) * s_B^2) / (n_A + n_B - 2), 1)

  tratio <- (mu_B - mu_A) / sqrt(s2_pool * (1/n_A + 1/n_B))

  if(abs(tratio) < 0.5 || abs(tratio) > 3.0)
    next

  Q <- quote(search(tgroups3, tgroups(n_A, mu_A, n_B, mu_B, s2_pool), .S, .R, .P, .E))
  S <- findall(Q, options = list(preproc = as.rolog), env = environment())

  if(problems(S))
    next

  break
}


tab <- data.frame(
  "Method A" = c(sprintf("%.0f", n_A), sprintf("%.1f", mu_A), sprintf("%.1f", s_A)), 
  "Method B" = c(sprintf("%.0f", n_B), sprintf("%.1f", mu_B), sprintf("%.1f", s_B)),
  check.names = FALSE
)

row.names(tab) <- c("Sample size", "Mean mathematics score", "Standard deviation")


t <- prepare(task=task, S)
sol <- format_feedback(
  t$correct, t$explanations, t$praise, t$blame, t$extra
)
```


Question
========
In a pedagogical study, researchers investigate whether AI-assisted learning is more effective 
than traditional tutoring sessions in improving mathematics performance. 
Students were randomly assigned to the two tutoring methods. 
Method A consisted of weekly tutoring session with a human tutor, 
whereas Method B involved AI-assisted learning using an adaptive learning platform. 
At the end of the semester, mathematics performance was assessed 
using a standardized mathematics achievement test, with higher scores indicating better performance. 
Consider the following data:

````{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(tab, align=c("c", "c", "l"))
````

The pooled sample variance is $s^2_\mathrm{pool}$ = `r s2_pool`.
Assuming equal population variances, 
calculate the $t$-statistic for the difference between the group averages.
A positive $t$-statistic ($t>0$) should indicate superiority of the AI-assisted learning group.

```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(t$alternatives, markup="markdown")
```

Solution
========
The $t$-statistic is calculated by: `r t$solution`

```{r solutionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
sol <- lapply(sol, FUN=gsub, pattern="\\n", replacement="")
answerlist(sol, markup="markdown")
```
